system.name: MadEye
system.one_liner: a live video analytics system that adaptively selects PTZ camera orientations to boost query accuracy

components.name: PTZ camera
components.role: captures frames and physically rotates to explore many orientations per timestep

components.name: Approximation models
components.role: cheap edge-compatible models that rank explored orientations by predicted workload accuracy

components.name: Search algorithm
components.role: selects which orientations to explore next using ranked orientations

components.name: Backend server
components.role: runs the accurate query models and manages training of the approximation models

components.name: Approximation model trainer
components.role: retrains the approximation models on samples from the backend

components.name: Query registration
components.role: accepts user query specifications (scene, model, objects, task)

components.name: Workload execution
components.role: runs the registered query on the best orientation's frames and returns results

components.name: User/App
components.role: registers queries and receives query results

content.key_idea: MadEye rapidly explores many PTZ orientations per timestep, uses lightweight approximation models to rank them, and continuously retrains those models from backend query results to keep selecting the most accurate camera configuration.
content.reading_order: left to right: from the PTZ camera's scene exploration loop, through the approximation-model/search-algorithm feedback loop, to the backend server's training and query-execution pipeline, ending at the user.

encoding.color_means: green = MadEye's own processing stages; small colored squares encode individual orientations that are explored, ranked, or selected
encoding.emphasis: the loop drawn between the camera, approximation models and search algorithm highlights the fast iterative orientation-exploration process at the core of the contribution

summary: MadEye boosts live video analytics accuracy by rapidly rotating a PTZ camera through many orientations each timestep and picking the one(s) that best serve the current query workload under resource limits. Figure 8 shows this end-to-end workflow as a left-to-right pipeline. On the left, the PTZ camera captures frames while a tight loop between it, a green 'Approximation models' box and a green 'Search algorithm' box explores orientations, ranks them with small colored squares, and feeds the ranking back to steer the next rotation. The best orientations are then sent right to a dashed 'Backend server' container holding 'Query registration', 'Workload execution' and 'Approximation model trainer' boxes: workload execution runs the real query models and returns results to a 'User/App' icon, while its outputs also become training samples that update the approximation models' weights, closing a second, slower feedback loop. Icons (camera, video thumbnails, people) and small color swatches make the data-heavy pipeline easier to follow.
summary_zh: 该图展示MadEye端到端流程：PTZ相机在探索算法与轻量近似模型之间循环，快速探索并排序多个拍摄朝向，选出最佳朝向后交由后端服务器执行查询、训练近似模型并向用户返回结果。
